column1: # `auto_restore`, spec §3.5. The default configuration has it on, so a finished word
# that is not a Vietnamese syllable is given back as the keystrokes that typed it.
# The engine decides at the word boundary, which the runner sends at the end of the
# A coda Vietnamese never spells: the marks have to go.
# An undone tone left a mark no syllable ends with.
# A letter modifier that produced a word no syllable spells.
# Words that are Vietnamese keep every mark.
# The undo of a modifier is not restored: the shown text is already what was typed,
# minus the key that undid the mark.
# The restore lands before the space, not after it.
# Limit of the rule, pinned so a later weakening of the tables fails here: `tét` is a
# real syllable (`nét`, `mét` and `sét` share its rhyme), so `auto_restore` must keep
# it. Typing English needs the language toggle, or `free_tone_mark` off.
